title: PSA: Ask your agent about implementing the window depth shader trick, aka "interior mapping". One of the best tricks in gamedev for cheap interiors.
author: sachasayan

replies.author: hypocrite_oath
replies.body: Maybe screen spaced reflection, for puddles on roads.

replies.author: PurpleKiwi
replies.body:
Graphics engineer here. There are way more than this, but here are some options:

- **Parallax occlusion mapping** - Bumpiness without more polygons
- **Subsurface Scattering** - For skin, leaves, and marble
- **Anisotropic Hair Shading** - For hair
- **Shell and Fin shader** - For fur
- **Volumetric Smoke/Fog/Clouds** - This can look way better and might even be cheaper than smoke particles in some cases
- **Cubemap and Screenspace Reflections** - Combine them since they cover each other's weaknesses
- **SSAO/contact Shadows** - Make objects not look like they're floating
- **PBR** - More realistic materials; Claude and GPT can both do this pretty well
- **Bloom** - Better looking bright stuff
- **DLSS/FSR** - This can double FPS with very little downside in many games
- **Antialiasing** - If stuff looks jagged/pixelated at edges
- **Light Baking** - In some games/engines this can be almost free at runtime, and you can get really good looking static lighting
- **Cascading Shadow Maps** - Shadows that can go far
- **Global Illumination** - Expensive but amazing-looking lighting with realistic bounces, though AI will take several attempts to get this right (it will probably attempt RTGI; you should ask for more options)

comments.author: Tramagust
comments.body: I mean cool it's implemented but why are all the rooms empty. It gives it a backrooms feel rather than making it feel good.

comments.author: SeaweedOk9985
comments.body:
I am using this in my game. I see you are making a rally game. Mine will have a driving component but I am going for a GTA 3 kind of feel.

Having so many buildings but with flat windows just seemed off. This half fixed the problem but I have a lot of tuning to do. For me, this shader trick is an LoD implementation. I am actually working to have every building have full walkable interiors (all 38k of them), so upclose players should be able to just see the real inside, but at a distance the shader trick will show a fake version of the actual interior.
